newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek deputy foreign minister resigns.
newsitem.headline: Greek deputy foreign minister resigns.

text.p: Deputy foreign minister Christos Rozakis resigned on Thursday following criticism from within the government of his conciliatory line towards Greece's longtime rival Turkey, officials said.
"Deputy foreign Minister Christos Rozakis submitted his resignation which was accepted," government spokesman Dimitris Reppas told reporters, adding that Rozakis's resignation was for health reasons.
"On December 18 he faced a heart attack and he was advised to abstain from his duties," Reppas said.
Government officials said Rozakis, a moderate professor of international law, was at odds with his boss, Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos, who backs a hard line against Ankara.
Rozakis, 55, was an advocate of a rapprochement with Turkey and supported closer relations between the European Union and Ankara, something that Pangalos has repeatedly vetoed.
He had also proposed a one-year extension of a moratorium agreed between Greece and Turkey which barred military exercises in the Aegean Sea during the summer months of last year.
Greece and Turkey came close to war last January over rights of an uninhabited islet in the Aegean. They are also at odds over the divided island of Cyprus.
Rozakis had also asked for the freezing of all military flights over Cyprus.
It was the first resignation of a government member at his level in the administration of socialist Prime Minister Costas Simitis, who won elections last September.
